title: Multi-AZ, read replicas and point-in-time recovery

videos.script: A database can fail in two ways. The machine can go, or somebody can make a mistake. They need different copies. {{two}} For the machine, there is Multi-AZ. A standby in another zone receives every write before the commit returns. When the primary fails, the name moves to the standby, and the application reconnects. {{standby}} For reading, there are read replicas. They answer queries, and they run a little behind, because they hear about each write only after it is committed. {{replica}} Neither one saves you from a DELETE without a WHERE. A replica copies the mistake a moment later. {{mistake}} For that, there are backups. A snapshot every day and the log every five minutes, so the database can be rebuilt at any second of the last week. {{backups}} And the restore surprises people. It does not rewind your database. It creates a new one, with a new address, beside the old. {{restore}} In moto you will make all of these, and watch each command succeed. Nothing replicates, nothing fails over and nothing is restored. You will learn exactly what to look for on a real account. {{moto}}
